learningObjective: Reason about when kernel launch overhead dominates and what mitigations exist.

requiredFeatures: CUDA driver launch cost ~ 5–10 μs per kernel

stem: Kernel launch overhead is typically ~5–10 μs on NVIDIA GPUs. Consider a training/inference loop dispatching many small kernels. Which of the following statements are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Kernel launch overhead is fully hidden by cudaStreamSynchronize because the CPU launch API is asynchronous; therefore small kernels do not suffer from launch overhead in practice.
Kernel fusion reduces per-op launch cost by combining multiple element-wise kernels into a single kernel, trading potential register pressure for a lower total launch count.
If a kernel executes for 2 μs and launch overhead is 5 μs, launch overhead dominates the wall time even at 100% GPU utilization; the effective GPU throughput is well below the kernel's peak.
CUDA Graphs capture a sequence of kernel launches once and replay them with a single API call, amortizing launch overhead across many small kernels.

explanation: A: When kernel duration < launch overhead, wall time is dominated by the CPU-side launch cost. This is the classic small-kernel regime. B: CUDA Graphs is precisely the mitigation: capture once, replay with a single graph-launch call, amortizing per-kernel overhead across the whole graph. D: Kernel fusion reduces the count of launches (also reduces HBM traffic when fused ops share operands). C is wrong: asynchronous launch does not eliminate the CPU cost of issuing a launch; every kernel still costs ~5–10 μs of CPU time. The GPU cannot begin work until the launch has been submitted.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: asynchronous launch means the CPU does not wait for kernel completion, but the launch itself still consumes CPU time and imposes a lower bound on inter-kernel spacing.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: kernel fusion cuts launch counts as one of its benefits, alongside reducing HBM traffic via operand reuse.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: when launch overhead > kernel time, the loop is CPU-bound on launches; the GPU sits idle much of the time.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: CUDA Graphs is the documented mechanism for amortizing per-launch overhead.

assumptions: Launch overhead ~5–10 μs per kernel is representative of recent CUDA driver stacks; small variations occur across versions.
The workload has a large number of short kernels (typical of decode-time transformer inference).
nonImplications: Does not imply CUDA Graphs is free; graph construction has one-time overhead and may not fit every dynamic control-flow pattern.
Does not imply fusion always improves performance; over-fusion can increase register pressure and reduce occupancy.

distractorRationales.A: Confuses asynchronous launch semantics with elimination of launch cost.

sourceRefs.locator: Streams, asynchronous launches, CUDA Graphs chapter
